lines.text: The ferry was late again, and the small crowd on the pier had begun to
drift towards the café, where the owner was already stacking chairs
against the rain. Agnes stayed by the railing with her suitcase.
Her brother did not answer at once. He watched the lights of the far
shore come on one by one, as if he were counting them, and then he
shrugged and picked up the heavier of the two bags.
The last boat of the season left the harbour at a
Nobody on board spoke much during the crossing. The engine was
loud, the benches were wet, and the captain kept the cabin door closed
against the wind until they reached the other side.
On the far side the road climbed steeply between stone walls, and by
the time they reached the house the rain had stopped and the sky over
the bay had turned a pale and washed-out green.
